outcomeNote: mishna stating law; no inter-party interaction

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִישׁ מַדִּיר אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּנָזִיר, וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מַדֶּרֶת אֶת בְּנָהּ בְּנָזִיר. כֵּיצַד? גִּילַּח, אוֹ שֶׁגִּילְּחוּהוּ קְרוֹבָיו. מִיחָה, אוֹ שֶׁמִּיחוּ קְרוֹבָיו.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «A man can vow» that «his» minor «son should be a nazirite,» i.e., a father can declare his son a nazirite, «but a woman cannot vow» that «her son should be a nazirite. How so;» what are the details of this naziriteship? If the son «shaved» his hair, thereby demonstrating his rejection of the vow imposed by his father; «or» if «his relatives shaved him;» or if the son «objected» by saying that he has no desire for this naziriteship; «or if his relatives objected» on his behalf, the naziriteship is canceled.

segments.he: הָיְתָה לוֹ בְּהֵמָה מוּפְרֶשֶׁת, הַחַטָּאת — תָּמוּת, וְהָעוֹלָה — תִּקְרַב עוֹלָה. וּשְׁלָמִים — יִקְרְבוּ שְׁלָמִים, וְנֶאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד, וְאֵינָן טְעוּנִין לֶחֶם.
segments.en: If this son who canceled the naziriteship «had animals separated» for his offerings, the one set aside for «the sin-offering must die, and the burnt-offering is sacrificed as a burnt-offering, and» the «peace-offering is sacrificed as a peace-offering. And» the peace-offering «is eaten for one day,» like the peace-offering of a nazirite, rather than the two days of a regular peace-offering, «and it does not require bread,» i.e., the loaves that accompany a nazirite’s peace-offering.

segments.he: הָיוּ לוֹ מָעוֹת סְתוּמִין — יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה. מָעוֹת מְפוֹרָשִׁים, דְּמֵי חַטָּאת — יֵלְכוּ לְיָם הַמֶּלַח, לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין. דְּמֵי עוֹלָה — יָבִיאוּ עוֹלָה, וּמוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן, דְּמֵי שְׁלָמִים — יָבִיאוּ שְׁלָמִים וְנֶאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד, וְאֵינָן טְעוּנִין לֶחֶם.
segments.en: If «he had unallocated funds,» they «will be allocated for» communal «gift» offerings. If he had «allocated funds» for his offerings, «the money for the sin-offering is taken» and cast «into the Dead Sea,» as one may «not benefit» from it ab initio, «but» if he benefits «from it,» he is «not» liable to bring an offering for «misuse» of consecrated property. With «the money for» the «burnt-offering they bring a burnt-offering;» it is prohibited to derive benefit from those coins «and» if he benefits «from it,» he is liable to bring an offering for «misuse» of consecrated property. With «the money for» the «peace-offering they bring a peace-offering, and» it «is eaten for one day and does not require bread.»

moves.summary: a father can make his son a nazirite, a mother cannot; shaving or protest cancels it
disposal of animals set aside for his offerings
disposal of unallocated and allocated funds

positions.claim: a man can impose naziriteship on his son but a woman cannot; if the son or relatives shave or protest it is canceled
set-aside animals and allocated funds are disposed of like those of a nazirite: sin-offering dies/to the Dead Sea, burnt- and peace-offerings are brought, peace-offering eaten one day without bread
